predefined_info.altitude: Elevation (m), clipped to your AOI. Continuous. Default source: [NASA SRTM 30 m](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/USGS_SRTMGL1_003). The advanced parameters offer [Copernicus GLO-30](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_DEM_GLO30) (© DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA) and [NASADEM](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/NASA_NASADEM_HGT_001).
predefined_info.slope: Terrain slope computed with Earth Engine's `ee.Terrain.slope`, in degrees by default or in percent (100 × the tangent of the angle; 45° = 100 %). Continuous. Same elevation sources as Altitude: [NASA SRTM 30 m](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/USGS_SRTMGL1_003) by default, [Copernicus GLO-30](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_DEM_GLO30) or [NASADEM](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/NASA_NASADEM_HGT_001) in the advanced parameters.
predefined_info.protected_area: Binary mask (1 = inside a protected area) built by rasterizing the polygons of the [WDPA — World Database on Protected Areas](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/WCMC_WDPA_current_polygons). By default: designated, inscribed, established and proposed sites, every IUCN category and designation type, marine areas included. The advanced parameters filter by status, IUCN category group, designation type and realm, and can add OECMs from the [WD-OECM](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/WCMC_WDOECM_current_polygons). Source: UNEP-WCMC and IUCN, Protected Planet. Set Period to By year for the network as of 31 December of a chosen year.
predefined_info.rivers: Binary mask of water from the [OSM Water Layer](https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/osm_water/), clipped to your AOI. By default large lakes and rivers, major rivers, canals and small streams count as water (ocean excluded); change the classes under Advanced parameters.
predefined_info.roads: Binary road mask (1 = road), clipped to your AOI. By default roads are rasterized from [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), with no breakdown by road type. Under *Advanced parameters* you can switch to **GRIP4**, the Global Roads Inventory Project (Meijer et al. 2018, [Environ. Res. Lett. 13 064006](https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aabd42); PBL/GLOBIO, CC BY 4.0, via the [awesome-gee-community-catalog](https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/grip/)), and choose which road types to keep. GRIP4 is a ~2018 snapshot compiled from national sources: it maps far fewer minor and unpaved roads than OSM and road-type definitions vary by country, so some AOIs have no roads of a given type (e.g. no highways).
predefined_info.forest_gfc: Forest/non-forest mask (1 = forest) for the chosen year, derived from [Hansen Global Forest Change](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/UMD_hansen_global_forest_change_2025_v1_13): pixels above the tree-cover threshold in 2000 minus loss up to that year. Temporal.
predefined_info.forest_tmf: Forest/non-forest mask (1 = forest) at 1 January of the chosen year from the [JRC Tropical Moist Forest](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/projects_JRC_TMF_v1_2024_AnnualChanges) annual-change product. By default only undisturbed forest counts; Advanced parameters can add degraded forest and regrowth. Temporal.
predefined_info.towns: Binary urban-area mask (1 = urban) for the nearest epoch, from [JRC GHSL](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/JRC_GHSL_P2023A_GHS_BUILT_S). Default: at least 15 people and 90 m² of built-up surface per 100 m cell (1975–2020). Advanced: the [GHSL settlement model (SMOD)](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/JRC_GHSL_P2023A_GHS_SMOD) degree-of-urbanisation classes at 1 km (1975–2030; 2025 and 2030 are GHSL projections). Temporal (5-year epochs).
predefined_info.subj: Categorical raster of administrative units from [FAO GAUL](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/FAO_GAUL_2015_level2) (2024 release): districts (level 2) by default, provinces (level 1) in the advanced parameters, each unit given a distinct value. Used for JNR-style stratification. Above 254 units the layer is downloaded as a 16-bit raster; JNR stratification separates at most 999 units.
predefined_info.precipitation: Total precipitation (mm) for the chosen year or month: the sum of the [ERA5-Land Monthly Aggregates](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/ECMWF_ERA5_LAND_MONTHLY_AGGR) totals (default, ~11 km) or of [CHIRPS Daily](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/UCSB-CHG_CHIRPS_DAILY) rainfall (~5.5 km, 50°S–50°N only). Data: Copernicus Climate Change Service / Climate Hazards Center UCSB. Continuous. Temporal.
predefined_info.temperature_2m: Air temperature at 2 m (°C) for the chosen year or month. A year combines the 12 monthly means of [ERA5-Land Monthly Aggregates](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/ECMWF_ERA5_LAND_MONTHLY_AGGR); a month combines its daily means from [ERA5-Land Daily Aggregates](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/ECMWF_ERA5_LAND_DAILY_AGGR), with the chosen aggregation metric (~11 km). Data: Copernicus Climate Change Service. Continuous. Temporal.
predefined_info.burned_area: Binary mask (1 = burned) of the pixels burned during the chosen year or month, from the monthly burned-area products [MODIS MCD64A1](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/MODIS_061_MCD64A1) (default, from Nov 2000) or [VIIRS VNP64A1](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/NASA_VIIRS_002_VNP64A1) (from Mar 2012), ~463 m. Data: NASA LP DAAC. Temporal.
predefined_info.active_fire: Active-fire detections in the chosen year or month: any detection (1 = fire), the number of fire days, or the maximum fire radiative power (MW). Sources: [MODIS MOD14A1 + MYD14A1](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/MODIS_061_MOD14A1) (Terra + Aqua, default), [VIIRS VNP14A1](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/NASA_VIIRS_002_VNP14A1) or [NASA FIRMS](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/FIRMS) (no radiative power), ~1 km. Data: NASA LP DAAC / NASA FIRMS (LANCE). Temporal.
predefined_info.fire_history: Fire history at the start of the chosen year or month, looking back the chosen number of years: how many of those 12-month spans had fire, or the whole years since the last fire (capped at the look-back). Built from [MODIS MCD64A1](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/MODIS_061_MCD64A1) burned area (default) or MODIS active fires, ~463 m / ~1 km. The period itself is never included, so the layer can explain a fire target of the same period. Data: NASA LP DAAC. Temporal.
predefined_info.dry_spell: Dryness at the start of the chosen year or month, from daily rainfall over the look-back window: days since the last day with at least the rain threshold (capped at the window), the number of dry days, or the total rain (mm). Sources: [CHIRPS Daily](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/UCSB-CHG_CHIRPS_DAILY) (default, ~5.5 km, covers 50°S–50°N only: AOIs outside get no data) or [ERA5-Land Daily Aggregates](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/ECMWF_ERA5_LAND_DAILY_AGGR) (~11 km, global). Results depend strongly on the source and the threshold. Data: Climate Hazards Center UCSB / Copernicus Climate Change Service. Temporal.
predefined_info.deforestation_gfc: Deforestation target for the chosen period: 1 = forest on 1 January of the start year (tree cover in 2000 at or above the threshold, no earlier loss) that [Hansen Global Forest Change](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/UMD_hansen_global_forest_change_2025_v1_13) records as lost before 1 January of the end year; 0 = forest that remained; no data = not forest at the start. Identical to the forest-loss layer the Process step builds from two Hansen forest layers. Source: Hansen/UMD/Google/USGS/NASA (Hansen et al. 2013, CC BY 4.0).
predefined_info.deforestation_tmf: Deforestation target for the chosen period from the [JRC Tropical Moist Forest](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/projects_JRC_TMF_v1_2024_AnnualChanges) annual changes: 1 = forest on 1 January of the start year (per the forest definition) that is deforested land, regrowth or new water by 1 January of the end year; 0 = forest still standing (degradation alone does not count); no data = not forest at the start. Source: JRC TMF v1 2024 (Vancutsem et al. 2021, Science Advances).
predefined_info.degradation_tmf: Degradation target for the chosen period from the JRC TMF annual changes: 1 = undisturbed forest on 1 January of the start year that is recorded as degraded in any year of the period (including forest degraded and then cleared); 0 = forest still undisturbed at the end; no data = anything else (not undisturbed at the start, or cleared without degradation). Source: JRC TMF v1 2024 (Vancutsem et al. 2021, Science Advances).
predefined_info.surface_water: Binary surface-water mask (1 = water) from [JRC Global Surface Water v1.4](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/JRC_GSW1_4_GlobalSurfaceWater) (Pekel et al. 2016, Nature 540: 418–422; 1984–2021, 30 m). A pixel counts when its water occurrence reaches the threshold and its transition class is one of the selected water types (permanent and seasonal by default). The dataset ends in 2021, so later changes are missing. Static.
predefined_info.mapbiomas_lulc: Annual land cover from [MapBiomas](https://mapbiomas.org) for the chosen region: Brazil (Collection 11, 1985-2025), Pan-Amazon (Collection 6, 1985-2023), Bolivia (Collection 3, 1985-2024), Colombia (Collection 2, 1985-2023), Ecuador (Collection 4, 1985-2025), Paraguay (Collection 3, 1985-2025), Peru (Collection 3, 1985-2024) or Venezuela (Collection 2, 1985-2023). The output is a 0/1 mask of the selected groups (forest, other natural vegetation, farming, non-vegetated, water) or one class per group. The AOI must lie inside the region. Data: MapBiomas, CC-BY-SA 4.0. Temporal.
predefined_info.deforestation_mapbiomas: Vegetation loss between two years from the MapBiomas deforestation and secondary-vegetation product: 1 = primary vegetation (optionally also secondary) at the start that was cleared before the end year, 0 = still standing, no data = not vegetation at the start. Regions: Brazil (Collection 11, intervals 1988-2026), Bolivia (Collection 3, 1986-2025), Paraguay (Collection 3, 1986-2026), Peru (Collection 3, 2000-2025). The AOI must lie inside the region. Data: MapBiomas, CC-BY-SA 4.0.
predefined_info.mapbiomas_fire: MapBiomas Fire for Brazil (Collection 5.1, 1985-2025), Colombia (2000-2025), Paraguay (1999-2024) and Peru (1990-2025): burned area for a year or a month, burn severity (Brazil only), years since the last fire, or the number of burned years in a look-back window before 1 January. The monthly Fire Monitor (Brazil, from January 2019) is an advanced source for recent months. Data: MapBiomas, CC-BY-SA 4.0. Temporal.
predefined_info.mapbiomas_degradation: Degradation indicators from MapBiomas Brazil (Collection 10.1): edge age (years the native vegetation has been at an edge, no data elsewhere, 1985-2024), secondary vegetation age (years since regrowth began, 0 = not secondary vegetation, 1985-2024), selective logging (1 = logged in the year, 1988-2024) and canopy disturbance frequency (number of disturbances, 1988-2024). The AOI must lie inside Brazil. Data: MapBiomas, CC-BY-SA 4.0. Temporal.
predefined_info.mapbiomas_water: Surface water from MapBiomas Water for Brazil (Collection 5, 1985-2025), Bolivia (Collection 4, 1985-2025) and Peru (Collection 3, 1985-2024, annual only): 1 = water in the year or in the chosen month, 0 = no water. Monthly maps run from January 1985 to December 2025. The AOI must lie inside the region. Data: MapBiomas, CC-BY-SA 4.0. Temporal.

modal.source_hint: Predefined = ready-made Earth Engine layers; User = your own raster, vector or GEE asset.
modal.param_tree_cover_threshold_hint: Minimum canopy cover in 2000 counted as forest (1-100). It becomes part of the variable name, so several thresholds can coexist.
modal.param_aggregation_hint: How the values are combined: the 12 monthly means for a whole year, or the daily means for a single month. It becomes part of the variable name, so several metrics can coexist.
modal.param_roads_source_hint: OpenStreetMap (default) is the most complete. GRIP4 (~2018) is sparser but lets you choose road types. A non-default source becomes part of the variable name (roads_grip).
modal.param_road_types_hint: GRIP4 road classes counted as road. A subset becomes part of the variable name, e.g. roads_grip_rhp = highways + primary roads. Types absent from your AOI give an all-zero layer.
modal.custom_type_hint: Local raster file = GeoTIFF on disk; Google Earth Engine asset = GEE asset; Local vector file = vector file, rasterized during harmonization.
modal.custom_year_hint: Set for temporal layers so the same variable can be added per year; leave blank for static ones.
modal.custom_scale_hint: Nominal pixel size in metres used when exporting this GEE asset.
modal.band_hint: This raster has {count} bands; the layer uses only the one picked here.
modal.custom_raster_type_hint: continuous = measured values (e.g. elevation); categorical = classes or 0/1 masks.
modal.stretch_hint: Reads the layer's percentiles (an Earth Engine asset over the AOI) and fills Min and Max. Leave both empty to stretch automatically.
modal.find_classes: Find the classes in the layer
modal.find_classes_hint: Lists the values found in a sample of the layer (an Earth Engine asset over the AOI). A rare value can be missed: add it by hand. Values not listed are transparent.
modal.find_features_hint: Lists one class per feature, in file order, named from the file's first text column; features not listed are transparent.
modal.err_too_many_features: More than 50 features: the layer is drawn with automatic colours.
modal.zero_one_note: Only 0 and 1 were found: 0 starts hidden (transparent). Click its eye to draw it.
modal.err_class_value: Enter a whole number not already listed.
modal.err_no_classes: Find the classes or add a value.
modal.err_duplicate_class: Each value can be listed once.
modal.err_class_limit: A categorical layer holds at most 50 classes.
modal.err_range: Min and Max must be numbers, Min below Max, or both empty.
modal.err_not_integer: This layer has non-integer values: set its raster type to continuous.
modal.err_too_many_classes: More than 50 values: this layer looks continuous.
modal.err_no_stretch: The layer has no spread of values.
modal.probe_failed: Could not read the layer's values: {error}
modal.custom_rasterization_method_hint: binary = 1 where a feature is present, 0 elsewhere; unique = one value per feature/class.
modal.error_no_predefined_selected: Select a variable from the list.
modal.error_year_required: Year is required for this variable.
modal.error_param_range: {label} must be a whole number between {min} and {max}.
modal.param_water_classes_hint: OSM Water Layer classes mapped as water (1). A non-default selection adds a code to the variable name (e.g. rivers_wlmc).
modal.param_tmf_definition_hint: TMF classes counted as forest. A non-default choice is added to the variable name (e.g. forest_tmf_degraded).
modal.error_param_multichoice: Select at least one option for {label}.
modal.param_period_hint: Whole year, or one calendar month of the chosen year. A month becomes part of the variable name (e.g. _sep), so one model per month can be built.
modal.param_burn_sensor_hint: MODIS MCD64A1 (from Nov 2000) or VIIRS VNP64A1 (from Mar 2012, detects more small burns). Both ~463 m.
modal.param_fire_metric_hint: Any detection gives a 0/1 mask; fire days counts the days with a detection; maximum radiative power is the strongest fire seen (MW).
modal.param_fire_confidence_hint: Lowest detection confidence counted as fire. The default keeps nominal and high confidence.
modal.param_fire_source_hint: MODIS Terra + Aqua (from Mar 2000), VIIRS (from Feb 2012) or NASA FIRMS (MODIS-based, no radiative power). All ~1 km.
modal.param_history_metric_hint: Fire years counts the 12-month spans with fire in the look-back; years since fire is the number of whole years since the last fire.
modal.param_history_window_hint: How many years before the period start are examined (1-20). It becomes part of the variable name.
modal.param_history_source_hint: MODIS burned area (MCD64A1, ~463 m) or MODIS active fires (~1 km, nominal and high confidence).
modal.param_dry_metric_hint: Days since rain counts the dry days just before the period start; dry days counts every dry day in the window; total rain sums the rain in the window.
modal.param_rain_threshold_hint: A day with at least this much rain counts as a rain day (1-50).
modal.param_dry_window_hint: Days before the period start that are examined (7-999). Days since rain is capped at this value.
modal.param_rain_source_hint: ERA5-Land (~11 km, global) or CHIRPS (~5.5 km, 50°S–50°N only; AOIs outside get no data).
modal.error_period_unavailable: No data for {year}: this layer needs {start} to {end}, and the selected source covers {first} to {last}. Pick another year, period or source.
modal.error_frp_firms: NASA FIRMS has no fire radiative power. Choose MODIS or VIIRS as the source, or another measure.
modal.param_start_year_hint: Forest is taken on 1 January of this year.
modal.param_end_year_hint: Events up to 31 December of the previous year count. Both years become part of the variable name.
modal.error_interval_order: The end year must be later than the start year.
modal.error_param_year: {label}: choose a year from the list.
modal.param_dem_hint: Digital elevation model the layer is computed from. SRTM (default) is the original NASA model, NASADEM a reprocessed SRTM and Copernicus GLO-30 a more recent radar model.
modal.param_slope_unit_hint: Degrees (0–90) or percent rise (100 × the tangent of the angle; 45° = 100 %).
modal.param_pa_timing_hint: Current: every site in today's WDPA, one map used for every period. By year: the sites designated by 31 December of the chosen year; sites with an unknown status year (about 7 %) count in every year, and boundaries are today's.
modal.param_pa_status_hint: WDPA legal status of the sites to include. The default keeps designated, inscribed, established and proposed sites; adopted sites are left out unless you add them.
modal.param_pa_site_types_hint: Protected areas (WDPA) and/or other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs, from the WD-OECM).
modal.param_pa_iucn_hint: IUCN management category groups to include. Sites without a category fall in the last group, as do all OECMs. With every group selected, nothing is filtered.
modal.pa_iucn_strict: Ia–II: strict reserves, wilderness, national parks
modal.pa_iucn_managed: III–IV: natural monuments, habitat and species management
modal.pa_iucn_unassigned: Not reported, not assigned or not applicable
modal.param_pa_designation_hint: National, regional or international designations (e.g. World Heritage, Ramsar). With all three selected, nothing is filtered.
modal.param_pa_realm_hint: Keep every site, or drop the sites recorded as marine. Coastal sites are always kept.
modal.param_towns_method_hint: Population and built-up thresholds on the 100 m GHSL grids (default), or GHSL settlement-model (SMOD) classes at 1 km.
modal.param_towns_population_hint: Minimum number of people per 100 m cell (1–999, default 15).
modal.param_towns_built_hint: Minimum built-up surface per 100 m cell, in m² (1–999, default 90).
modal.param_towns_smod_classes_hint: SMOD classes counted as urban. The default is the GHSL urban domain: urban centre, dense, semi-dense and suburban.
modal.param_subj_level_hint: Districts (GAUL level 2, default) or provinces (GAUL level 1). Large AOIs can hold hundreds of districts; the download then switches to 16-bit automatically.
modal.param_sw_occurrence_hint: Share of the 1984–2021 observations in which the pixel was water (1–100, default 1). Raise it to keep only reliably wet pixels.
modal.param_sw_types_hint: JRC transition classes counted as water: permanent (including new and seasonal-to-permanent), seasonal (including new and permanent-to-seasonal) and ephemeral. Lost water never counts.
modal.param_mapbiomas_region_hint: MapBiomas collection that covers the AOI. Pre-selected from the AOI country; the download stops if the AOI is not inside it.
modal.param_lulc_mode_hint: A 0/1 mask of the selected groups, or a map with one class per group.
modal.param_lulc_groups_hint: Pixels whose MapBiomas class belongs to one of these groups get 1, the others 0.
modal.param_fire_product_hint: Burned area, burn severity, years since the last fire, or number of burned years.
modal.param_fire_window_hint: Years before 1 January of the selected year that are searched. A pixel never burned in the window gets window + 1.
modal.param_mapbiomas_fire_source_hint: Fire Monitor gives recent months (Brazil, from January 2019) before they reach the annual collection.
modal.param_defo_vegetation_hint: Primary vegetation only, or also secondary (regrown) vegetation.
modal.param_degradation_variable_hint: Which MapBiomas degradation indicator to map.

subj_notice.wide: {name}: {n} administrative units, saved as a 16-bit raster so that each unit keeps its own value.
subj_notice.wide_jnr: {name}: {n} administrative units, saved as a 16-bit raster. JNR stratification separates at most 999 units: use the province level or a smaller AOI for JNR models.

mapbiomas.error_outside_region: Only {pct}% of the AOI is inside MapBiomas {region} (at least {min}% is needed). Choose the MapBiomas region that contains the AOI.
mapbiomas.error_year: MapBiomas {region} has this layer from {first} to {last}.
mapbiomas.error_period: MapBiomas {region} has this layer from {first} to {last} (year-month).
mapbiomas.error_not_available: This option is not available for MapBiomas {region}.
mapbiomas.error_interval_range: MapBiomas {region} deforestation intervals can start in {first} at the earliest and end in {last} at the latest.
